items.headline: Tech Sector Leads Market Decline Amid AI Spending Worries and Surging Oil Prices
items.summary: U.S. equities concluded Thursday's session broadly lower, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite experiencing significant losses. Investor sentiment was dampened by concerns over substantial AI infrastructure spending revealed in major tech earnings, coupled with rising crude oil prices due to escalating geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. Defensive sectors, including Consumer Staples and Health Care, showed resilience amidst the broader market retreat, suggesting a rotation away from growth stocks. Not financial advice.

items.headline: Allegion Surges on Rotation and Earnings Outlook
items.summary: Allegion PLC ($ALLE) jumped 10.31% to $174.15, marking the top intraday performer in the S&P 500. This rally occurred despite an overall market decline and may reflect investor rotation into industrial and security solutions ahead of its earnings release.

items.headline: Wisesat Space Holdings Leads Smaller Cap Gains
items.summary: Wisesat Space Holdings ($SAIQ) saw a significant surge, rising 37.4% to $7.64 during today's trading.

items.headline: Biohaven Shares Climb on Strong Performance
items.summary: Biohaven Ltd. ($BHVN) experienced a notable increase of 24.7%, closing at $14.65.

items.headline: Avalo Therapeutics Plunges
items.summary: Avalo Therapeutics, Inc. ($AVTX) was among the biggest decliners today, dropping 36.5%.

items.headline: NVE Corp. Sees Steep Decline
items.summary: NVE Corp. ($NVEC) shares fell sharply, down 32.9% by midday.

items.headline: Meta Platforms Shares Slide on AI Spending Concerns
items.summary: Meta Platforms ($META) fell 5.89% to $656.41. Despite reporting a strong quarter, the tech giant's negative free cash flow for the first time since 2012, amidst an 80% year-on-year increase in AI infrastructure spending, unnerved investors.

items.headline: Technology Sector Leads Market Selloff as AI Doubts Resurface
items.summary: The technology sector experienced a significant downturn today, with the Nasdaq Composite falling over 2%. This decline was largely driven by renewed investor concerns about the substantial costs associated with AI investments and unclear timelines for profitability, especially following earnings reports from major tech companies.

items.headline: Oil Prices Surge to Five-Month High Amidst Middle East Tensions
items.summary: Crude oil prices climbed, with Brent crude touching $113 a barrel, nearing a five-month high. The increase is attributed to ongoing geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, sparking fears of supply disruptions and a wider regional conflict, which is adding to inflationary concerns.

items.headline: Defensive Sectors Show Strength Amidst Market Volatility
items.summary: Amidst the broader market decline, defensive sectors like Consumer Staples, Health Care, and Utilities demonstrated relative strength. The Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR Fund ($XLP) rose 2.09%, and the Health Care Select Sector SPDR Fund ($XLV) gained 1.47%, indicating a rotation of capital into more stable areas of the market.

items.headline: U.S. Jobless Claims Fall to Three-Month Low, Signaling Stable Labor Market
items.summary: Economic data released today showed that U.S. initial jobless claims unexpectedly fell to a historically low 194,000, reaching its lowest point in three months. This suggests continued stability in the labor market, even as continuing claims saw a slight increase.

items.headline: Federal Reserve Meeting Next Week with Focus on Rate Hike Probabilities
items.summary: The Federal Reserve is scheduled to meet next week, October 27-28. Market probabilities indicate an 18% chance of a rate increase at that meeting, with a higher 75% probability for a rate hike in December.
